notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2024 (matches data.js fy 'Dec 2024'). Spotify reports under IFRS in euros, so values are billions of EUR (converted from € millions, no FX). Source is the FY2024 Form 20-F (filed February 5, 2025, accession 0001639920-25-000003); stock comp matches SEC XBRL. OWNERSHIP is as of December 31, 2024, from Item 7.A. LEADER, PROXY SHARES: Ek's 29,105,267 ordinary shares (14.3%) are what the 20-F reports as his beneficial ownership. They include shares he only votes. Footnote (1) says 12,473,298 are held by D.G.E. Investments, which he owns indirectly, and that he votes the shares held by TME Hong Kong, Image Frame, Tencent Mobility Limited and Distribution Pool Limited (all Tencent entities, 16,631,969 shares) through an irrevocable proxy held by D.G.E. Investments. 12,473,298 + 16,631,969 = 29,105,267, so the Tencent shares are inside his 14.3%. For reference only (computed, not stated in the filing): 12,473,298 / 203,844,409 is about 6.1%. TENCENT is listed in the 20-F at 16,631,969 ordinary shares, 8.2%. It is not added to largestHolders because those shares are already counted in Ek's figure (overlap rule). BENEFICIARY CERTIFICATES: Ek holds 124,732,980 (38.4%) and Lorentzon 200,000,000 (61.6%). They carry votes but no economic rights and are excluded from economic percentages. Ek's 29.1% voting power is as stated; the 20-F shows a dash for Tencent's voting power because Ek votes those shares. HOLDERS: Lorentzon's 9.8% includes 45,566 option shares exercisable within 60 days. Baillie Gifford's row relies on a Schedule 13G/A filed November 5, 2024, with no as-of date given, so asOf is null. DIVIDENDS: none ever paid. BUYBACKS: no repurchases in 2024 (a dash in the 2024 column; €2 million in 2022). PLAN: none described in the sections read.

ecosystem.notes: The 20-F states no total for royalties paid to rights holders: it says "Cost of revenue consists predominantly of royalty and distribution costs related to content streaming" but does not break royalties out, so payouts is null. The $10 billion is Spotify's own figure from its Loud & Clear 2025 report, in US dollars (the filing reports in euros), and is money paid to the music industry as a whole (rights holders such as labels and publishers, not only artists; the Loud & Clear site says its lifetime total "includes both recording and publishing royalties"). It is not audited filing data. No volume measure exists, so measure is null.

footprint.notes: Two kinds of country data. (1) The 20-F itemises 2024 average employees only for the U.S., Sweden and the U.K.; it gives approximately 1,730 'employees and contractors' in aggregate across about 25 other countries, which is not a country row. (2) Loud & Clear: the 2025 edition (2024 data) is no longer on loudandclear.byspotify.com, which now shows the 2026 edition (2025 data). Country figures for 2024 were taken from Spotify's own newsroom posts for that edition: Sweden (over SEK 1.9 billion; the Swedish source writes '1,9 miljarder kronor' with a decimal comma), Brazil (over BRL 1.6 billion), Canada (nearly CAD 460 million) and the EU (€1.7 billion). Royalties are by artist origin, paid to rights holders, not to artists directly. Each currency is its own metric; they are not comparable or additive. Sweden has two rows because the employee and royalty figures come from different documents. India's 2024 post gives no amount, and the EU post's 'Italy became a $100M+ market' is ambiguous, so neither is recorded. Office lease space comes from Item 4.D (occupied space is lower: about 226,000 and 378,000 sq ft). No U.S. state data.
